Change c0246. Location: 1818 Vol. II, Ch. V; 1831 Ch. XIII.

Context before (unchanged): "I now hasten to the more moving part of my story.

1818 text: I shall relate events that impressed me with feelings which, from what I was, have made me what I am.

1831 text: I shall relate events, that impressed me with feelings which, from what I had been, have made me what I am.

Diff: I shall relate events {+,+} that impressed me with feelings which, from what I [-was-] {+had been+} , have made me what I am.

Context after (unchanged): "Spring advanced rapidly; the weather became fine, and the skies cloudless.

result.rationale: Changes 'from what I was' to 'from what I had been' and adds a comma; the past-perfect shift is a grammatical/syntactic refinement that keeps the meaning of the narrator's self-transformation, though it slightly sharpens the sense of a completed former state.
